clue.text: No East End gangster given bird

indicators.note: 'No' with 'End' asks for the gangster's name to lose a letter at its tail

parts.note: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A gangster from somewhere other than London's East End is handed a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No East End' says the gangster's name has no E (East) at its end: CAPONE becomes CAPON. 'End' finishes the deletion signal begun by 'No'; the East End is London's cockney district, a false lead here.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table, a type of domestic fowl.

clue.text: Bad-tempered taxi driver run in

indicators.note: 'run in' asks for the letter for run to be placed inside the driver

parts.note: a cabby is a driver of a taxi cab
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A grumpy cab driver gets pulled in for a traffic offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby is an informal synonym for irritable and grumpy.

clue.text: American lout making an appearance in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: 'in Pennsylvania' says the state's abbreviation is wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Pennsylvania
an gives the indefinite article A
a look is an appearance, as in 'the look of the place'

explanation.surface: An American thug turns up somewhere in Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: Palooka is US slang for a clumsy, stupid oaf, often a second-rate boxer.

clue.text: After fifteen days, character's not finished book

indicators.note: 'After' places the trimmed character behind the days in the finished word

parts.note: fifteen days are half of November's thirty, so the first half of the word NOVEMBER

indicators.note: something not finished lacks its final part, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a letter is a written character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: After two weeks, a fictional character is still incomplete, as is the book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifteen days' is half of November, so take the first half of the word NOVEMBER, NOVE. 'not finished' drops the R of LETTER, leaving LETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel, a slim work of fiction.

clue.text: Person in court mentioned minor instance of air rage?

indicators.note: 'mentioned' says the words are spoken and the answer is what they sound like

parts.note: a small quarrel aboard an aircraft is a plane tiff

explanation.surface: Someone in court refers to a small bout of passenger fury on a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: A tiff is a petty quarrel, so a minor flare-up of air rage is a plane tiff, which said out loud matches the legal word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party bringing a civil action in a court of law.

clue.text: Little angel proving a true oaf when going off the rails

indicators.note: a train going off the rails is wrecked, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A supposedly good child turns out to be a real lout once they misbehave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off the rails' rearranges PROVING A TRUE OAF into the three-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-behaved child is often called a little angel, a model of goodness.

clue.text: Air current in December is novel

explanation.surface: A tune that is popular in December happens to be a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: An air is a tune and current means popular, so a song popular in December is a carol at Christmas; the second definition is Dickens's story.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasonal song sung in December; also Dickens's festive book about Scrooge.

clue.text: Rock musician finally appeared half cut

indicators.note: 'finally' picks out the closing letter of the word musician
with half cut away, only the opening half of the word appeared is kept

explanation.surface: A rock musician finally shows up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it trims APPEARED to its first half, APPE.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology a nappe is a large sheet of rock thrust over younger strata.

clue.text: I married partner, gathering round a cleric's office

indicators.note: 'gathering round' means the pieces before it enclose the little word a

parts.note: a mate is a partner or spouse

explanation.surface: Someone tells of marrying their partner, a ceremony performed by a religious official.
explanation.definitionFit: An imamate is the office or rank of an imam, a Muslim religious leader.

clue.text: Leaders of feudal regime need me to reform slaves no longer

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters
to reform is to reshape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The heads of a medieval regime need someone to change things for freed slaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges NEED ME into EEDMEN, after FR from the opening letters of feudal and regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedmen were people released from slavery, formerly enslaved and now emancipated.

clue.text: Everywhere is in a state of disorder

explanation.surface: Something found everywhere is in a complete mess.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means scattered in every location, and also chaotic or muddled.

clue.text: Illegally sell port by the gallon

parts.note: Bootle is a port town on the Mersey beside Liverpool

explanation.surface: Someone sells port wine illicitly in bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the fortified wine, but it is BOOTLE, a dock town on Merseyside in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To bootleg is to make or trade goods, especially liquor, unlawfully.

clue.text: Whence Bjork single, recording that contains style

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit

indicators.note: 'that contains' means the recording is wrapped around the style

parts.note: a CD, compact disc, is a recording
elan is flair or style

explanation.surface: Bjork's single comes on a disc with real flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single' suggests a pop release, fitting Bjork, but it gives I, the Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer Bjork comes from this North Atlantic island nation, so it is where she hails from.

clue.text: French girl with little time for strict disciplinarian

parts.note: Martine is a French female first name
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A French girl has little time for a strict teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a person who demands rigid obedience to rules, named after a French drillmaster.

clue.text: Line from a letter read aloud

indicators.note: 'read aloud' means the letter is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: the letter here is Q, the seventeenth of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A line taken from a letter is read out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' suggests correspondence, but it is a letter of the alphabet, Q, whose name matches the word for a line of waiting people.
explanation.definitionFit: A queue is a line of people waiting their turn.

clue.text: Victoria sponge?

parts.note: Victoria was a queen, so a sponge named after her is a small cake fit for royalty

explanation.surface: A request for a classic British jam-filled layer cake.
explanation.walkthrough: A Victoria sponge is the classic British jam sandwich cake; reading Victoria as the monarch gives a small cake named for a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen cake is a small currant cake, here taken as a cake belonging to a monarch like Victoria.

clue.text: Supports star player on baseball team

parts.note: backs means supports, as in backing a candidate
top means star or best, as in a top player

explanation.surface: A fan cheers for the star of the baseball side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star player' reads as one phrase, but 'star' gives TOP and 'player on baseball team' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball a backstop is the catcher, the fielder stationed behind home plate.

clue.text: Brokeback Mountain director briefly expressed point of view

indicators.note: 'briefly' cuts the director's name short by its last letter

parts.note: Ang Lee directed the 2005 film Brokeback Mountain

explanation.surface: The director of a famous film states his outlook in a few words.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is a particular perspective or slant on a subject.

clue.text: Great to unwind a length of wire

indicators.note: to unwind is to undo coils, so these letters come loose and rearrange

explanation.surface: It is great to relax with a piece of wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwind' means relax on the surface but rearranges GREAT TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A garotte is a cord or wire used for strangling.

clue.text: Dance music appears loud to injured officer

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical direction meaning loud
lame means injured, unable to walk properly
NCO is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: Dance music sounds noisy to a wounded soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the passionate Andalusian style of song, guitar and dance.

clue.text: Expression of surprise by man on board preparing food

parts.note: coo is a British exclamation of surprise
the king is a piece on a chessboard

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at a man on a ship who is making a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship, but it is a chessboard and the man is the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking is the making of meals, the act of getting dishes ready to eat.

clue.text: Famous actor, typical househusband?

explanation.surface: A celebrated film star is the model of a stay-at-home husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Newman was the Hollywood star; a 'new man' is a man who shares housework and childcare.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Newman was a celebrated Hollywood star; a modern domestic male shares chores at home.

clue.text: Capital once invested in Ankara, chiefly

indicators.note: 'invested in' says the answer is tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Money was once put mainly into the Turkish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks financial with 'invested', but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Karachi was Pakistan's capital until the seat of government moved in the late 1950s.

clue.text: Woman takes Conservative peer round House of Lords

indicators.note: 'round' says the peer's name surrounds the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, the former athlete, sits as a Conservative peer in the Lords
HL is the abbreviation for House of Lords

explanation.surface: A woman takes a Tory lord on a tour of Parliament's upper chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Coe, Olympic runner and former Conservative MP, is the peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloe is a female first name, so any woman might bear it.

clue.text: Approve of criminal getting convicted

parts.note: con is short for convict, a criminal
done is British slang for convicted, as in 'done for theft'

explanation.surface: Someone accepts that a lawbreaker was found guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to accept or overlook wrongdoing, tacitly sanctioning it.

clue.text: A NATO militarist sorted out a system of government

indicators.note: something sorted out is rearranged into order, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A warmonger in the Atlantic alliance has redesigned a political regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges A NATO MILITARIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Totalitarianism is a dictatorial regime demanding complete subservience to the state.

clue.text: Heard quiet male becoming animated bit by bit

indicators.note: 'Heard' says the word for quiet is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: peace means quiet, as in peace and quiet

indicators.note: becoming animated means springing into lively motion, so these letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: A calm man is heard slowly coming to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' turns PEACE (quiet) into its sound-alike PIECE; 'becoming animated' rearranges MALE into MEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means gradually, a little at a time.

clue.text: Gielgud Centre in Scottish town

indicators.note: the centre of the actor's surname is its middle three letters

explanation.surface: The actor's name is on a centre in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: John Gielgud was a great English actor; ELG is the middle of his name. ELGIN is a town in Moray in north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a cathedral town in Moray, in northern Scotland.
